title: [D4 Rendering] Triage rendering builder — the five-part bounded projection
summary: `helena/rendering/` is the fourth versioned package: `__init__.py` reads one context out of the engine into an unformatted `ContextProjection` (five queries), and `v1.py` turns that plus a `helena.hosts` attribute set into a `helena.contracts.v1.Rendering` — the five closed sections, one line per record, every claim carrying its stable evidence identifier and every lookup carrying its status. `sql/migrations/0016_triage_rendering_inputs.sql` adds the one thing the engine did not expose, `helena_signal_context_tls`, and `docs/decisions/0018-the-triage-rendering.md` records the TLS parameter subset and the criterion that chose it, the line grammar, and the six things the rendering deliberately does not carry.
assumption_validated: That the five parts of `concept/04` can be built from what the store already holds, and that `stale` / `failed` / `missing` / `no_match` survive into the text a model reads rather than collapsing at the last layer. Both hold, and both are demonstrated against a real capture and a real ThreatFox load rather than argued: the four statuses reach four lines that are not each other, and the pair the whole stage exists to keep apart — `sslbl-ja3 status=missing` on a fingerprint nobody could look up, `threatfox status=ok classification=no_match` on a domain that was looked up and is not listed — is one rendering away from being one word. ONE NEGATIVE RESULT, and it is the useful one: the first draft took the entity list from `helena_analytical_enriched_context` and it was WRONG. That view's source list is the snapshot ledger, so before any feed has ever loaded it yields no rows at all, and the rendering showed a host that contacted nothing on a deployment whose only fault was that no loader had run. The tests caught it (nine failures on the first run, all of them 'this entity does not appear'). The entity list is `helena_signal_context_entities`' and the claims are the analytical view's. What is NOT demonstrated is that this shape reads well to a small fast model — no model has been given one — nor that the rendering is bounded, which it is not yet.
makes_buildable: Task 29 has the two things a size budget needs and nothing it has to undo: a neutral record order — `(entity_type, entity_value)`, deliberately not hits-first, because truncation over a hits-first order drops the negative space — and a measurement, 4 964 characters for the ten-record layer-coverage capture in one window with no feed loaded and 5 886 after a load with one hit. A record is exactly one line, so `Truncation.kept` / `total` are line counts and a dropped record cannot separate a claim from its entity. Tasks 30-31 have the object to put in `AgentRequest.rendering`: `rendering.RenderingStore(connection, identity).project(context_id)` then `rendering.version('v1').render(projection, hosts.load().attributes_for(host))`, and the request's two copies of `rendering_version` are already asserted equal by the contract. D5 has `rendering.version(identifier)` as the replay path for a stored `rendering_version`, and `ContextProjection.context_version` as the thing `AgentRequest.context_version` is filled from.

verification.detail: 963 passed in 484 s (911 before this task; 52 new, of which 48 are tests/test_rendering.py and the rest are the two retrofits and one new test in tests/test_hosts.py). The engine tests run against a migrated schema on a throwaway in-memory ./bin/risingwave, ingest the ten-record layer-coverage capture through the real normalizer with its `ts` re-stamped into the current window, and load a real ThreatFox extract through the real loader. `uv lock --check` and `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` are both clean; no dependency was added. MUTATION-CHECKED THREE TIMES, each restored byte-identically (md5 verified) and re-run green. (1) Collapsing `status` and `classification` into one token — `outcome = record.classification or record.status` — fails exactly five, including test_missing_and_no_match_are_two_different_lines and test_the_four_statuses_are_four_different_renderings. (2) Changing the tier filter from `(evidence_tier IS NULL OR evidence_tier = %s)` to a plain equality fails ten, including both arms: the stand-in-relation test that proves an `analyst` row is excluded, and every test that needs a `no_match` row to survive. (3) Dropping the minted `missing` record for a source with no rows fails five, including test_a_source_that_never_loaded_renders_missing_and_not_a_clean_record.
verification.first_run_note: Nine of the engine tests failed on their first run, and the failure was real rather than a test bug — see `assumption_validated`. The design changed; the tests did not.

escalations.detail: `concept/04` asks part two for a domain's "type or class" and part three for "service identification", and NO SOURCE IN THIS REPOSITORY SUPPLIES EITHER. `helena.enrichment.SOURCES` holds ThreatFox and SSLBL; Netify — which docs/decisions/0009-netify-application-identification.md cleared as a Tier D source of exactly this, with a million rows sitting in data/netify/ — has no loader and no descriptor. Registering one is an enrichment-source decision (concept/instruction.md §3), not part of a rendering task, so it was not done. What part three carries in the meantime is the destination ports the host actually reached, which is observed service identification rather than an absent feed's; part two carries nothing of the kind and says so by omission. Not blocking: the rendering is complete without it and a `v2` adds a field.

A URL-scoped claim is invisible to triage under rendering v1, and 287 of the 4 095 indicators in the ThreatFox snapshot are `url`-typed. `concept/04`'s five parts have no place for a URL record, and folding one into the domain section would need the host-part extraction re-implemented in the renderer when it already has exactly one home (sql/migrations/0010). `helena.rendering.v1.UNRENDERED_ENTITY_TYPES` names it rather than skipping it, and `render` raises if a declared entity type is ever neither rendered nor named there. What covers most of the gap is that the URL's host is already a domain record carrying `http` among its layers — measured on the layer-coverage capture, all five hosts of its six URL entities are. Recorded rather than decided: closing it is a rendering v2 or an enrichment view that also attaches a URL claim to its host.

The rendering carries the MAPPED claim and not the publisher's native payload — no malware name, no tags, no reporter, no reference URL, although `helena_reference_evidence.native_evidence` holds all of them. This is an isolation decision, not a formatting one: concept/instruction.md §6 says retrieved provider text is data and the isolation must be tested, and triage is a small fast model on the high-volume path with no tools and no way to check anything it is told, so feed text in that position is an instruction channel an indicator author can write to. What is rendered instead is the taxonomy path from a closed vocabulary, the numeric confidence, the scope, the tier, the timestamps and the evidence identifier — which is how the analyst tier or a human reaches the native record. Recorded because it is a judgement about what an agent may see: a rendering v2 that carries native text needs an isolation test before it needs a format.

deferred: THE SIZE BUDGET AND EVERY TRUNCATION. No section produced here carries a `Truncation`, and a test asserts that rather than leaving it to be noticed — `concept/08` lists the numeric budget values as open and `concept/07` makes budget values policy rather than constants in a branch. Task 29 is the increment titled for it. What this one supplies is the two things it needs: one record per line, and a neutral order. The maturity label says `not yet bounded` in both module docstrings.
Application identity and service identification for parts two and three. See the first escalation.
URL entities. See the second escalation.

A source's `caveat`. `SourceDescriptor.caveat` is 600 characters for `sslbl-ja3` and it is real and relevant — a list its own publisher says is untested against known-good traffic. It is deferred rather than dropped: the tier IS rendered, which is the governed strength signal, and a paragraph per source is a budget decision that belongs with the budget.

The reason a load failed. `status=failed` is rendered and is distinct from `missing`; *why* it failed is on `helena_reference_feed_snapshot.failure_reason`, which sql/migrations/0015 does not project. It would make an operator-facing status actionable and changes nothing a triage verdict turns on.

The negotiated ALPN protocol values. Not in the store at all — `helena_flatten_tls` carries `alpn_count` and not the values — so selecting it would be a flatten-layer change no note asks for. Recorded in ADR-0018 §3 as rejected for absence rather than by the criterion.

Wiring the renderer into `helena.orchestration`. `concept/03` puts rendering inside Orchestration ("renders agent input"), and orchestration is still the 13-line placeholder it was: nothing calls `render` outside the test suite, because the thing that would call it is the triage runner (task 31).

Storing a rendering. No assessment table exists (task 26 deferred it to D5), so `rendering_version` is recorded on a `Rendering` and an `AgentRequest` in memory and has not been written onto a citable row. concept/instruction.md §7's 'versions recorded on every citable row' stays open for the agent layer exactly as tasks 26 and 27 left it.

A second copy of `RENDERING_VERSION` in SQL. There is none — nothing in the engine renders anything — so there is no pair of constants to assert equal, unlike `AGGREGATION_VERSION`. `ENRICHMENT_TIER` IS such a pair (Python here, a literal in sql/migrations/0014) and is asserted equal by asking the engine what the evidence view produces.
lessons: task 28: THE ENRICHED CONTEXT DOES NOT ANSWER 'WHAT ENTITIES ARE THERE'. `helena_analytical_enriched_context` CROSS JOINs the entities against `SELECT DISTINCT source_id FROM helena_reference_feed_snapshot`, so with an empty ledger it yields ZERO ROWS for a context full of entities — task 25 recorded the same mechanism from the other side (deleting the only ledger row makes a source vanish). A rendering built on it shows a host that contacted nothing on any deployment where no loader has run yet. Take the entity list from `helena_signal_context_entities` and the claims from the analytical view, and join them in Python; absence of a claim row for a registered source then means exactly 'never asked', which is the `missing` status.

task 28: THE VIEW THAT ANSWERS THE COMPOSITION RULE IS NOT THE VIEW THAT ANSWERS THE RENDERING. sql/migrations/0015 projects three of the five observation flags because three is what the scope rule reads. Measured on the layer-coverage capture, three names are observed only by one of the two it leaves out — `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` and `ocsp.digicert.com` in an HTTP request URI and nowhere else, `106.137.52.in-addr.arpa` in a DNS response and nowhere else — so through those three flags they render as observed by no layer at all. Reading the signal view fixes it with no migration; an earlier draft of this task added one, retrofitted `Superseded by:` into 0015 for it, and backed the whole thing out once the entity list moved.

task 28: STATUS IS CONSTANT PER (CONTEXT, SOURCE) AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE RENDERING AFFORDABLE. A 64-character snapshot digest per record would be the same fact thirty times over, so freshness is stated once in a per-source section header — and the renderer RAISES if two entities in one window report different statuses or snapshots from one source, which is what makes the header true rather than approximately true. The per-record `status=` is deliberately kept beside it: the two cannot drift, and a reader is at the record when the question arises.

task 28: FILTERING ON `evidence_tier` NEEDS THE NULL ARM. `evidence_tier` reaches the enriched context through a LEFT JOIN, so it is NULL on exactly the rows that carry no claim — every `no_match`, `missing` and `failed`. `WHERE evidence_tier = 'enrichment'` drops all of them and leaves a rendering of nothing but hits, which is the same misreading as one showing none. Mutation-checked: the plain equality fails ten tests.

task 28: A TIER-FILTER TEST CAN BE EXECUTED WITHOUT A PRODUCER FOR THE OTHER TIER. Nothing in this repository writes an `analyst`-tier row — the tier is a literal in sql/migrations/0014 — so the query is exposed as `rendering.ENRICHMENT_QUERY` and run against a stand-in TABLE of the same name and column shape in a pristine `engine_schema`, holding one row of each tier plus one with a NULL tier. That executes the real predicate against a real engine instead of grepping the string, and it is a reusable trick for any filter whose excluded case has no producer yet.

task 28: `tests/test_view_layering.py` CHECKS `Read by:` COMPLETENESS FOR RELATIONS but only existence for files. Adding a view means retrofitting the `Read by:` block of every relation it reads — 0005 and 0006 here — and their checksums move, with the cost docs/runbook.md describes. Outside readers (modules, tests) are not checked for completeness, so `Read by:` lists of Python files drift and several were already stale ('nothing renders a context yet', 'the enriched-context view (D3) is the next reader'); those two were false after this task and were corrected.

task 28: `tests/test_hosts.py::test_nothing_outside_the_package_mints_a_host_attribute` FORBADE A TYPE ANNOTATION. Task 27's AST scan refuses the name `HostAttributes` anywhere in `src/helena` outside the package, and `def render(projection, attributes: hosts.HostAttributes)` trips it. The test was widened to skip nodes inside an annotation subtree (`ast.arg.annotation`, `ast.AnnAssign.annotation`, `FunctionDef.returns`), with a new test proving that a call in an annotated assignment is still caught. Naming a type is not producing one; the rest of the scan is intact.

task 28: MEASURED — one host, ten flows, one 5-minute window renders to 4 964 characters over the five sections with no feed loaded and 5 886 after a load with one hit. 14 domains, 15 addresses, 6 fingerprints, 6 URLs (unrendered) and two distinct TLS parameter tuples. The enrichment adds about 19 % to a rendering and one hit adds 190 characters. That is the number task 29's budget starts from, and it is a QUIET host: the fixture is two minutes of one Windows endpoint.

task 28: The real TLS values in the sample are `client_version=0303`, `server_version=0303`, `server_cipher=C030`/`C02F` — the sensor's own hex, not names. They are rendered as they arrived; a version/cipher-suite name table is an external fact this repository does not hold, and inventing one is the class of error the project has already had to correct.
task 28: The full suite is now 963 tests in ~480 s on this machine (911 before). Budget a session against that.
failed_approaches: task 28: Building the rendering's entity list from `helena_analytical_enriched_context`. WRITTEN, TESTED, AND FOUND WRONG BY THE TESTS — nine engine tests failed on their first run with 'this entity appears on 0 lines'. The view's source list is the snapshot ledger, so a store where no feed has loaded produces no rows at all and the rendering claimed the host contacted nothing. Do not retry it; the split is in ADR-0018 §1 and in the head of sql/migrations/0016.

task 28: Migration 0016 as a DROP-and-recreate of `helena_analytical_enriched_context` adding the two missing observation flags and `fingerprint_algorithm`, with `Superseded by: 0016` retrofitted into 0015. Written in full and backed out: once the entity list has to come from `helena_signal_context_entities` anyway, those columns come with it and the migration buys nothing but a checksum break and 110 lines of duplicated SQL including the port-matching join. 0016 now creates exactly one object and supersedes none.

task 28: Rendering the snapshot version and load time on every enriched record. Rejected before it was committed — the digest is 64 characters and the fact is constant per (window, source), so it is a per-source header line instead. The renderer refuses to write that header if any two records disagree, which is what makes the compression safe rather than merely cheap.

task 28: Collapsing `status` and `classification` into one token to save room on a line. Considered and refused for the obvious reason, then MUTATION-CHECKED to prove the suite would catch it: five tests fail, including the one that puts `status=missing` and `status=ok classification=no_match` side by side in a single rendering.
next_session_should_know: Task 29 bounds this rendering, and the shape is ready for it. Four things to carry. (1) A RECORD IS EXACTLY ONE LINE and the enrichment of a record is appended to that record's own line behind ` | `, so `Truncation.kept`/`total` are line counts and no budget can keep an entity while dropping its claim. Do not move a claim onto a continuation line. (2) THE ORDER IS `(entity_type, entity_value)` AND IT IS NEUTRAL ON PURPOSE. Task 25's warning applies directly: an enriched context is mostly negative space, and a truncation over a hits-first order hands triage a store that looks like nothing but threats. If you choose a selection order under the budget, choose it deliberately and write down what it does to the negative space; ADR-0018 §9 records the current order and why. (3) THE MEASUREMENT IS 4 964 CHARACTERS for one quiet host's five-minute window with no feed loaded, 5 886 after a load with one hit; the fixture is two minutes of one Windows endpoint, so the busy-host number the PRD asks you to instrument is still unmeasured. (4) `Truncation` refuses a record that dropped nothing, and `check_exchange` refuses an outcome with no `truncated` gap when the rendering truncated — so the moment you emit one, the triage runner must emit the gap. `tests/test_rendering.py::test_no_section_claims_to_have_been_truncated` is the assertion that will have to change, and it says so in its docstring. Two API notes: `rendering.RenderingStore(connection, identity).project(context_id)` raises `helena.context.ContextOutsideRetention` for a context outside the boundary, so every engine test here re-stamps the capture into the current window the way tests/test_context.py does — a fixture dated 2024-06-01 renders nothing. And `helena/rendering/` may hold only `__init__.py` and `vN.py`; the machinery (the queries, the row models, the loader) is in `__init__.py` and the format is in `v1.py`, which is frozen the moment a row records `rendering_version = "v1"`. One unrelated correction landed in this commit: `tests/test_view_layering.py::test_the_repository_records_every_definition_the_engine_does_not_hold` said "Seven, all of them 0010's" and the map it asserts has ten entries; the docstring now says ten.
